readings.title: Jeremiah Imprisoned by Zedekiah
readings.subtitle: The prophet is confined for prophesying the fall of Jerusalem.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 32:1] The word that came to Yirmeyahu from <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in the tenth year of Tsiḏqiyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, which was the eighteenth year of Neḇuḵaḏretstsar.
[2] Now at that time the army of the sovereign of Baḇel besieged Yerushalayim, and Yirmeyahu the prophet was shut up in the court of the guard, which was in the house of the sovereign of Yehuḏah.
[3] For Tsiḏqiyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah had shut him up, saying, “Why are you prophesying, saying, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am giving <dn>את</dn> this city into the hand of the sovereign of Baḇel, and he shall take it,</dq>
[4] <dq>and Tsiḏqiyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah shall not escape from the hand of the Kasdim, but certainly be given into the hand of the sovereign of Baḇel, and shall speak with him face to face, and see him eye to eye,</dq>
[5] <dq>and he shall lead Tsiḏqiyahu to Baḇel, and be there until <dn>I</dn> visit <dn>את</dn> him,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“though you fight with the Kasdim, you shall not prosper”</dq> ’?”

readings.title: A Field in Anathoth
readings.subtitle: As a sign of future restoration, Jeremiah buys his cousin's field.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 32:6] And Yirmeyahu said, “The word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying,
[7] <dq>See, Ḥaname’ěl son of Shallum your uncle is coming to you, saying, “Buy <dn>את</dn> my field which is in Anathoth, for the right of redemption is yours to buy it.” ’</dq>
[8] “So Ḥaname’ěl my uncle’s son came to me in the court of the guard according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said to me, ‘Please buy <dn>את</dn> my field that is in Anathoth, which is in the land of Binyamin, for the right of inheritance is yours, and the redemption. Buy it for yourself.’ And <dn>I</dn> knew that this was the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[9] “And <dn>I</dn> bought <dn>את</dn> the field which was at Anathoth from Ḥaname’ěl, my uncle’s son, and weighed out to him <dn>את</dn> the silver, seventeen sheqels of silver.
[10] “And <dn>I</dn> signed <dn>את</dn> the deed and sealed it, took <dn>את</dn> witnesses, and weighed <dn>את</dn> the silver in the scales.
[11] “Then <dn>I</dn> took <dn>את</dn> the deed of purchase – that which was sealed according to the command and law, and that which was open –
[12] and <dn>I</dn> gave <dn>את</dn> the deed of purchase to Baruḵ son of Něriyah, son of Maḥsěyah, in the presence of Ḥaname’ěl my uncle’s son, and in the presence of the witnesses who signed the deed of purchase, before all the Yehuḏim who sat in the court of the guard.
[13] “And <dn>I</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> Baruḵ before their eyes, saying,
[14] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>“Take <dn>את</dn> these deeds, both this deed of purchase which is sealed and this deed which is open, and put them in an earthen vessel, so that they remain many days.”</dq>
[15] For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>“Houses and fields and vineyards shall again be bought in this land.”</dq> ’

readings.title: Jeremiah's Prayer of Perplexity
readings.subtitle: The prophet questions the command to buy land while the city is under siege.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 32:16] “And after <dn>I</dn> had given <dn>את</dn> the deed of purchase to Baruḵ son of Něriyah, <dn>I</dn> prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying,
[17] Ah, Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! See, <dn>You</dn> have made <dn>את</dn> the heavens and <dn>את</dn> the earth by <dn>Your</dn> great power and outstretched arm. There is no matter too hard for <dn>You</dn>,
[18] who show loving-commitment to thousands, and repay the crookedness of the fathers into the bosom of their children after them – the Great, the Mighty <dn>Ěl</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts is <dn>His</dn> Name,
[19] great in counsel and mighty in work, for <dn>Your</dn> eyes are open to all the ways of the sons of men, to give everyone according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds.
[20] For <dn>You</dn> have set <dn>את</dn> signs and wonders in the land of Mitsrayim, to this day, and in Yisra’ěl and among other men. And <dn>You</dn> have made <dn>Yourself</dn> a Name, as it is this day.
[21] And <dn>You</dn> have brought <dn>את</dn> Your people Yisra’ěl out of the land of Mitsrayim with signs and wonders, with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and with great fearsome deeds.
[22] And <dn>You</dn> gave them <dn>את</dn> this land, of which <dn>You</dn> swore to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
[23] And they came in and possessed it, but they did not obey <dn>Your</dn> voice nor did they walk in <dn>Your</dn> Torah. They did not do all that <dn>You</dn> commanded them to do, so <dn>You</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> all this evil upon them.
[24] See the siege mounds! They have come to the city to take it. And the city has been given into the hand of the Kasdim who fight against it, because of the sword and the scarcity of food and the pestilence. And what <dn>You</dn> have spoken has come about, and look, <dn>You</dn> see it!
[25] Yet <dn>You</dn>, O Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have said to me, <dq>“Buy <dn>את</dn> the field for silver, and take <dn>את</dn> witnesses”!</dq> although the city has been given into the hand of the Kasdim.’ ”

readings.title: YeHoVaH's Reply: Judgment is Certain
readings.subtitle: The Lord recounts the persistent idolatry that has sealed Jerusalem's fate.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 32:26] Then the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yirmeyahu, saying,
[27] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of all flesh. Is there any matter too hard for <dn>Me</dn>?”</dq>
[28] Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am giving <dn>את</dn> this city into the hand of the Kasdim, into the hand of Neḇuḵaḏretstsar sovereign of Baḇel, and he shall take it.</dq>
[29] <dq>“And the Kasdim who fight against this city shall come and set fire to <dn>את</dn> this city and burn <dn>את</dn> it, with the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to Ba‛al and poured out drink offerings to other mighty ones, to provoke <dn>Me</dn>.</dq>
[30] <dq>“For the children of Yisra’ěl and the children of Yehuḏah have done only evil before <dn>Me</dn>, from their youth. For the children of Yisra’ěl have only provoked <dn>Me</dn> with the work of their hands,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[31] <dq>“For this city has been a cause for <dn>My</dn> displeasure and <dn>My</dn> wrath from the day that they built it, even to this day that <dn>I</dn> should remove <dn>את</dn> it from before <dn>My</dn> face,</dq>
[32] <dq>because of all the evil of the children of Yisra’ěl and the children of Yehuḏah, which they have done to provoke <dn>Me</dn> – they, their sovereigns, their heads, their priests, their prophets, and the men of Yehuḏah, and the inhabitants of Yerushalayim.</dq>
[33] <dq>“And they have turned their back to <dn>Me</dn>, and not their face – though <dn>I</dn> taught them, rising up early and teaching them, they did not listen to receive instruction.</dq>
[34] <dq>“And they set <dn>את</dn> their abominations in the house which is called by <dn>My</dn> Name, to defile it.</dq>
[35] <dq>“And they built the high places of Ba‛al which are in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, to offer up their sons and their daughters to Moleḵ, which <dn>I</dn> did not command them, nor did it come into <dn>My</dn> heart, that they should do this abomination, to make Yehuḏah sin.</dq>

readings.title: The Promise of Restoration
readings.subtitle: Despite the coming exile, YeHoVaH promises to gather His people and make an everlasting covenant.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 32:36] “And now, thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, concerning this city of which you say, ‘It shall be given into the hand of the sovereign of Baḇel by the sword, and by scarcity of food, and by pestilence’:
[37] <dq>See, <dn>I</dn> am gathering <dn>את</dn> them out of all the lands where <dn>I</dn> have driven them in <dn>My</dn> displeasure, and in <dn>My</dn> wrath, and in great rage. And <dn>I</dn> shall bring them back to <dn>את</dn> this place, and shall let them dwell in safety.</dq>
[38] <dq>And they shall be <dn>My</dn> people, and <dn>I</dn> shall be their <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq>
[39] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall give them one heart and one way, to fear <dn>Me</dn> all the days, for the good of them and of their children after them.</dq>
[40] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall make an everlasting covenant with <dn>את</dn> them, that <dn>I</dn> do not turn back from doing good to them. And <dn>I</dn> shall put <dn>My</dn> fear in their hearts so as not to turn aside from <dn>Me</dn>.</dq>
[41] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall rejoice over them to do good to them, and shall plant <dn>את</dn> them in this land in truth, with all <dn>My</dn> heart and with all <dn>My</dn> being.’</dq>
[42] “For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘As <dn>I</dn> have brought <dn>את</dn> all this great evil on this people, so <dn>I</dn> am bringing on them <dn>את</dn> all the good that <dn>I</dn> am speaking to them.</dq>
[43] <dq>And fields shall be bought in this land of which you are saying, “It is a wasteland, without man or beast. It has been given into the hand of the Kasdim.”</dq>
[44] <dq>Fields shall be bought for silver, and deeds signed and sealed, and witnesses be called, in the land of Binyamin, and in the places around Yerushalayim, and in the cities of Yehuḏah, and in the cities of the mountains, and in the cities of the low country, and in the cities of the South. For <dn>I</dn> shall turn back their captivity,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”

readings.title: Healing for a Broken City
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH promises to cleanse and restore Judah and Israel, making them a name of joy.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 33:1] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yirmeyahu a second time, while he was still shut up in the court of the guard, saying,
[2] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who made <dn>את</dn> it, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who formed <dn>את</dn> it to establish it, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is <dn>His</dn> Name,
[3] <dq>Call unto <dn>Me</dn>, and <dn>I</dn> shall answer you, and show you great and inaccessible matters, which you have not known.’</dq>
[4] “For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, concerning the houses of this city and the houses of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah, which are thrown down against the siege mounds and the sword,
[5] while coming to fight with the Kasdim, and to fill their places with the corpses of men whom <dn>I</dn> shall strike in <dn>My</dn> displeasure and <dn>My</dn> wrath, all for whose evil <dn>I</dn> have hidden <dn>My</dn> face from this city.
[6] <dq>See, <dn>I</dn> am bringing to it relief and healing. And <dn>I</dn> shall heal them and reveal to them the riches of peace and truth.</dq>
[7] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall turn back <dn>את</dn> the captivity of Yehuḏah and <dn>את</dn> the captivity of Yisra’ěl, and shall build them as at the first,</dq>
[8] <dq>and shall cleanse <dn>את</dn> them from all their crookedness that they have sinned against <dn>Me</dn>. And <dn>I</dn> shall pardon <dn>את</dn> all their crookednesses that they have sinned and by which they have transgressed against <dn>Me</dn>.</dq>
[9] <dq>And it shall be to <dn>Me</dn> a name of joy, a praise, and a pride before all nations of the earth, who hear all the good <dn>I</dn> am doing to them, and they shall fear and tremble for all the goodness and all the peace <dn>I</dn> am doing to it.’</dq>

readings.title: The Voice of Joy Returns
readings.subtitle: The desolate streets will once again be filled with gladness, praise, and flourishing flocks.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 33:10] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘In this place of which you say, “It is dried up, without man and without beast,” in the cities of Yehuḏah, in the streets of Yerushalayim that are deserted, without man and without inhabitant and without beast, there shall once again be heard</dq>
[11] <dq>the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the voice of those who are saying, “Praise <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is good, for <dn>His</dn> loving-commitment is forever,” of those who are bringing <dn>את</dn> the offering of praise into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. For <dn>I</dn> shall turn back <dn>את</dn> the captivity of the land, as at the first,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[12] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>‘In this place which is dried up, without man and without beast, and in all its cities, there shall once again be a home of shepherds causing their flocks to lie down.</dq>
[13] <dq>In the cities of the mountains, in the cities of the low country, and in the cities of the South, and in the land of Binyamin, and in the places around Yerushalayim, and in the cities of Yehuḏah, the flocks once again pass under the hands of him who counts them,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Righteous Branch of David
readings.subtitle: The covenant with David and the Levitical priesthood will be established forever.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 33:14] <dq>See, the days are coming,’</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘when <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> the good word which <dn>I</dn> have promised to the house of Yisra’ěl and to the house of Yehuḏah:</dq>
[15] <dq>In those days and at that time <dn>I</dn> cause a Branch of righteousness to spring forth for Daviḏ. And <dn>He</dn> shall do right-ruling and righteousness in the earth.</dq>
[16] <dq>In those days Yehuḏah shall be saved, and Yerushalayim dwell in safety. And this is that which shall be proclaimed to her: ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our Righteousness.’</dq>
[17] “For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘For Daviḏ there is not to cease a man to sit on the throne of the house of Yisra’ěl.</dq>
[18] <dq>And for the priests, the Lěvites, there is not to cease a man to offer ascending offerings before <dn>Me</dn>, to kindle grain offerings, and to slaughter continually.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: An Unbreakable Covenant
readings.subtitle: As surely as day and night, YeHoVaH will not reject His people or the line of David.
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 33:19] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yirmeyahu, saying,
[20] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘If you could break <dn>את</dn> My covenant with <dn>את</dn> the day and <dn>את</dn> My covenant with <dn>את</dn> the night, so that there be not day and night in their season,</dq>
[21] <dq>then <dn>My</dn> covenant could also be broken with <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ <dn>My</dn> servant – so that he shall not have a son to reign upon his throne – and with <dn>את</dn> the Lěvites, the priests, <dn>My</dn> attendants.</dq>
[22] <dq>As the host of the heavens is not counted, nor the sand of the sea measured, so <dn>I</dn> increase <dn>את</dn> the descendants of Daviḏ <dn>My</dn> servant and the Lěvites who attend upon <dn>Me</dn>.’ ”</dq>
[23] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yirmeyahu, saying,
[24] “Have you not observed what these people have spoken, saying, ‘The two clans which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has chosen have been rejected by <dn>Him</dn>’? So they have despised <dn>My</dn> people, no more to be a nation before them.
[25] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘If <dn>My</dn> covenant is not with day and night, and if <dn>I</dn> have not appointed the laws of the heavens and earth,</dq>
[26] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> would also reject <dn>את</dn> the descendants of Ya‛aqoḇ and Daviḏ <dn>My</dn> servant, so that <dn>I</dn> should not take of his descendants to be rulers over the descendants of Aḇraham, Yitsḥaq, and Ya‛aqoḇ. For <dn>I</dn> shall turn back <dn>את</dn> their captivity, and have compassion on them.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Judgment for Gloating
readings.subtitle: Because Tyre rejoiced over Jerusalem's fall, she will become plunder for the nations.
readings.text:
[Ezekiel 26:1] And it came to be in the eleventh year, on the first of the new moon, the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying,
[2] “Son of man, because Tsor has spoken against Yerushalayim, ‘Aha! She, the gateway of the peoples, has been broken, she has been turned over to me. Let me be filled, she has been ruined.’
[3] “Therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘See, <dn>I</dn> am against you, O Tsor, and shall cause many nations to come up against you, as the sea causes its waves to come up.</dq>
[4] <dq>And they shall destroy <dn>את</dn> the walls of Tsor, and they shall break down <dn>את</dn> her towers. And <dn>I</dn> shall scrape <dn>את</dn> her dust from her, and shall make her like a shining rock.</dq>
[5] <dq>She shall be a place for spreading nets in the midst of the sea, for <dn>I</dn> have spoken,’</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>‘And she shall become plunder for the nations,</dq>
[6] <dq>while her daughter villages which are in the fields are killed by the sword. And they shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’</dq>

readings.title: The Destroyer from the North
readings.subtitle: Nebuchadnezzar will utterly demolish Tyre, leaving it a bare rock for spreading nets.
readings.text:
[Ezekiel 26:7] “For thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘See, <dn>I</dn> am bringing against Tsor from the north Neḇuḵaḏretstsar sovereign of Baḇel, a sovereign of sovereigns, with horses, and with chariots, and with horsemen, even an assembly, and many people.</dq>
[8] <dq>With the sword he shall kill <dn>את</dn> your daughters in the field. And he shall heap up a siege mound against you, and shall build a wall against you, and shall raise a large shield against you,</dq>
[9] <dq>and set <dn>את</dn> the blow of his battering rams against your walls, and break down <dn>את</dn> your towers with his weapons.</dq>
[10] <dq>From his many horses, their dust shall cover you. From the noise of the horsemen, and vehicles, and chariots, your walls shall shake as he enters your gates, as men enter a city that is breached.</dq>
[11] <dq>With the hooves of his horses he tramples <dn>את</dn> all your streets, he kills <dn>את</dn> your people by the sword, and <dn>את</dn> the columns of your strength shall fall to the ground.</dq>
[12] <dq>And they shall plunder <dn>את</dn> your riches, and they shall loot <dn>את</dn> your merchandise. And they shall break down <dn>את</dn> your walls and destroy <dn>את</dn> your pleasant houses. And they shall put <dn>את</dn> your stones, and <dn>את</dn> your timber, and <dn>את</dn> your dust in the midst of the water.</dq>
[13] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall cause <dn>את</dn> the sound of your songs to cease, and let the sound of your lyres be heard no more.</dq>
[14] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall make you like a shining rock, and let you be a place for spreading nets, never to be rebuilt, for <dn>I</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> have spoken,’</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
